chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Hafs ibn Qurt, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is more engaged with the world, his regret would be more intense during its separation.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of being overly attached to the world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the psychological burden of 'shubak' (entanglement), where deep worldly attachment intensifies the existential regret at the moment of parting. This concept is central to Shia asceticism (zuhd), emphasizing that the pain of separation is proportional to the depth of one's emotional investment in transient matters. It serves as a practical warning for believers to cultivate detachment while engaging with the world to ensure a peaceful transition to the hereafter.
